BYJU’S insolvency: Kerala Police register FIR against GLAS Trust over alleged lender document forgery
Complaint alleges a disputed authorisation letter was used to support a ₹11,432.98 crore claim and 99.41% voting rights in the edtech company's insolvency proceedings.
ETEducation
Published On Nov 04, 2026 at 01:34 AM IST
Set ETEducation as your preferred source on Google
Bookmark
Comment
The complaint seeks preservation and production of the original electronic document and related email communications from GLAS TrustKerala Police have registered a criminal case against GLAS Trust Company LLC and others over allegations of forgery and cheating linked to the insolvency proceedings of Think & Learn Private Limited, the parent company of edtech company BYJU’S.
The case follows a complaint by Rajendran Vellappalath, managing director of Voizzit Technology Private Limited, alleging that a lender authorisation letter dated July 25, 2024, was fabricated and subsequently used to establish GLAS Trust's authority to represent lenders during the insolvency process.
According to a petitioners' bench note filed before the Kerala High Court, the disputed document allegedly reused signatures from an earlier authorisation letter dated January 18, 2024, while changing lender details, dates and amounts.

The petitioners have also alleged that certain amounts were inserted as electronic document comments rather than appearing on the signed pages, and that signature images were copied across multiple pages. They have sought examination of the original electronic files to establish the document's authenticity and modification history.
Dispute over ₹11,432 crore lender claim
The authenticity of the authorisation letter is significant because it allegedly formed the basis for recognising GLAS Trust's authority to represent lenders in BYJU’S insolvency proceedings.
The petitioners contend that GLAS Trust required authorisation from lenders representing more than 50% of the relevant loan exposure. They further argue that excluding the disputed signature pages would bring the claimed lender support down from approximately 95% to 42%, potentially raising questions over the validity of the authorisation.
Complainant seeks forensic examination
The complaint seeks preservation and production of the original electronic document and related email communications from GLAS Trust, insolvency professionals and Microsoft. It also seeks examination of the electronic material by the Cyber Forensic Division of the State Forensic Science Laboratory in Thiruvananthapuram.
The proposed examination is intended to establish how the document was created and modified, and whether the disputed signatures, dates and amounts were altered or reused.
The registration of the FIR brings the allegations into the criminal investigation process. However, the claims remain allegations made by the complainant and petitioners and have not been established through forensic findings or judicial determination
